reason: Start building rocky planetesimals by bringing the stone and metal mixture together gently.
expectation: The grains may stick into larger rocky aggregates, though further steps will probably be needed for planetesimals.

alternatives.reason: I also considered starting with icy material, but chose the rocky route first.

effect: Rocky pebbles have formed, but simple sticking alone will not reliably take them much further.
reaction: The bouncing and fragmentation limit makes the next growth problem interesting.
reason: Continue the rocky route by seeing how gas drag affects the pebbles.
expectation: Gas drag may alter the pebbles' orbits and help concentrate them, though the mechanism is not yet clear.

alternatives.reason: I considered starting icy pebbles, but prefer to follow the rocky route first.

effect: Gas drag makes the rocky pebbles drift, potentially concentrating them in structured regions.
reaction: The link between orbital drift and concentration is useful.
reason: Use the pressure maximum to try to gather the drifting pebbles into a denser swarm.
expectation: The pressure maximum may concentrate the pebbles, bringing them closer to gravitational collapse.

alternatives.reason: I considered starting the icy route, but want to continue the rocky one first.

effect: The pressure maximum concentrated the rocky solids, setting up gravitational growth without relying on every collision sticking.
reaction: It's satisfying to see how concentration bypasses the sticking problem.
reason: Apply gravity to the dense swarm to pursue rocky planetesimals.
expectation: The swarm may collapse into rocky planetesimals, though it could require another stage.

alternatives.reason: I considered starting the icy route, but want to finish the rocky route first.

effect: The dense rocky swarm collapsed into planetesimals, completing the rocky goal; the icy goal remains.
reaction: It's satisfying to see gravity turn the accumulated solids into substantial bodies.
reason: Start the icy route with the only offered combination.
expectation: Gentle collisions will likely form icy aggregates or pebbles, analogous to the rocky route.

effect: Icy pebbles have formed, carrying both rock and volatile material.
reaction: The parallel with the rocky route is clear, though predictable.
reason: Follow the only offered combination to advance the icy route.
expectation: Gas drag will likely cause the icy pebbles to drift, as it did for rocky pebbles.

effect: Gas drag concentrated the icy solids through collective feedback, unlike the rocky route's pressure trap; the swarm is ready for gravity.
reaction: The different concentration mechanism was a useful surprise.
reason: Apply gravity to the icy swarm using the only offered combination.
expectation: The concentrated swarm will likely collapse into icy planetesimals and complete the remaining goal.

effect: Gravity bound the icy swarm into planetesimals, completing the remaining goal; these bodies are possible water carriers, not the sole source of terrestrial hydrogen.
reaction: The completed icy route was satisfying, especially with that qualification about water sources.

mostWorthwhile.text: Concentrating the rocky pebbles in a pressure trap and then using gravity showed a useful way around the limits of sticking.

leastWorthwhile.text: Starting the icy route felt repetitive at first because its gentle-collision step closely paralleled the rocky route.

surprise.text: Gas drag concentrated the icy swarm through collective feedback, rather than using the rocky route's pressure trap.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, although the compatible-option menu made the later choices largely prescribed rather than discoveries.

continue.text: Yes. The contrasting ways to concentrate solids made me curious how these small bodies grow into worlds, although I would hope for more meaningful choices.
